lead: Garland plumbing deals with clay soil, slab foundations and homes from the 1960s to 1980s. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Garland.
risk: slab leaks from shifting clay, aging water heaters and burst pipes in hard freezes
risk_short: slab leaks, water heaters and frozen pipes
why: Much of Garland was built from the 1960s to the 1980s. Copper lines under those slabs and cast-iron drains are aging, and expansive clay moves with every dry summer and wet spring.
Rare hard freezes, like February 2021, burst attic and exterior-wall pipes. Many homes are on their second or third water heater.
water: Garland buys treated water mainly from the North Texas Municipal Water District, which draws from Lavon Lake and other regional lakes. The water is moderately hard.
tips: Water your foundation evenly in dry summers.
Scope cast-iron drains in older homes.
Replace water heaters past 10 to 15 years.
areas: PipeMend works in Downtown Garland, Firewheel, Eastern Hills, Club Hill, Spring Park, Oakridge, Duck Creek and every other Garland neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Garland Building Inspection Department, and plumbers must hold a Texas license.

faq.q: Do Garland homes have cast-iron drains?
faq.a: Many homes built before the mid-1970s do. After 50 years, cast iron can crack or rot from the inside, causing slow drains and backups. A camera inspection shows its condition.
